title: Rello: make consistency the *lead*
dek: The one-page founder-facing version of the full Rello Creative Test Autopsy. It credits the current work, names one visible gap, and shows two test directions.
lens: Protein bar · creatine routine · active Meta creative
sources: Rello site + Meta Ad Library + NSF

sections.heading: the message *gap*
sections.body:
Rello's current ads give the buyer a real product difference: 20g protein plus 1.2g creatine, backed by clean-label language and lo-fi creator delivery. Four active ads found September 3 repeat the same primary text and near-identical creator treatment.

That does not prove fatigue or underperformance. It does reveal a clean next question: can the brand acquire more attention by leading with the routine problem its own origin story already names?

rows.claim: Rello is actively running paid social.
rows.evidence: Four active Meta ads were observed with start dates between August 12 and August 18, 2026. They repeat the same primary product copy.

rows.claim: The product and offer are live.
rows.evidence: Chocolate Crunch is listed at $53.99 for 12 bars with 20g protein, 1.2g creatine, and 9g fiber per bar.

rows.claim: Reduced routine friction is owned brand language.
rows.evidence: Rello says nutrition should not feel like a second job and contrasts its format with powders, scoops, and separate products.

items.why: Lead with the creatine-aware buyer who keeps forgetting a separate scoop. Show the bar entering a bag while the tub stays on the counter. The product facts become proof after the routine tension.

items.action: B · The protein bar with a performance layer
items.why: Lead with the solution-aware protein-bar buyer comparing labels. Make 20g protein plus 1.2g creatine the entire first-screen difference. Hold the broader benefit stack for the landing page.

blocks.label: Concept A · consistency
blocks.text:
A1  If the hardest part of creatine is remembering the scoop, put it in the snack you already carry.

A2  My protein bar started replacing one more tub on the counter.

A3  20 grams of protein. 1.2 grams of creatine. No shaker bottle.

blocks.label: Concept B · product difference
blocks.text:
B1  Most protein bars stop at protein. This one adds 1.2 grams of creatine.

B2  The label is short. The job list is not.

B3  A performance bar for people who are done managing a supplement stack.

sections.heading: visible *unknowns*
sections.body:
UNCONFIRMED: spend, sales, winning-ad status, CPA, ROAS, audience mix, customer objections, creator rights, margin, inventory depth, and approved claims.

The public evidence supports a test recommendation, not a diagnosis. Active does not mean winning. Repeated copy does not prove fatigue. Brand review must resolve the product page's 1g versus 1.2g FAQ wording before copy is finalized.
